name: Anti-communism
summary: Anti-communism is opposition to communism and Soviet-style rule, held by liberals, conservatives, Catholics, social democrats and fascists alike. Mainstream strands defend free markets, private property and elected government against central planning, class struggle and one-party dictatorship, while other strands have backed authoritarian regimes and mass repression in its name.
scope: A composite of the mainstream Cold War Western strand: Truman Doctrine containment, Hayek's critique of planning and Pius XI's Catholic rejection of communism. Anti-communism is a stance that cuts across ideologies, so on issues beyond communism itself the camp is split and many answers are low or 0; the fascist, authoritarian and counter-revolutionary strands are noted but not the centre.
